问题：7.1.1 General Neutralization Procedures相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Do neutralizations in a fume hood behind a safety shield, as vapors and heat may be generated. Wear lab coat or apron, gloves and goggles. A face shield in combination with safety goggles is recommended. Please note, a face shield alone is not sufficient, safety goggles must be worn when using a face shield. Keep containers cool during process, such as placing a beaker in a bucket with slushy ice. After neutralization is complete, dispose of down the drain followed by 20 parts water to the neutralized solution. Follow the specific neutralization procedures below for the acid or base you are trying to neutralize.

标题：Cornell Hazardous Waste Manual - 7.1.5 Hydrofluoric Acid
类别：废弃物
子类别：危险废物手册
实验室类型：通用
风险等级：4
危险类型：危险废物;标签;暂存;处置;卫星积累区
适用场景：参考Cornell University EHS公开资料处理危险废物手册相关实验室安全问题
问题：7.1.5 Hydrofluoric Acid相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Hydrofluoric acid is a strong corrosive and highly toxic chemical that causes severe burns from dilute solutions and can be fatal upon exposure of concentrated solutions. Bench top use of hydrofluoric acid is not permitted; it must only be used in a fume hood. Anyone using Hydrofluoric acid must contact the Gannett Health Center and purchase a tube of Calcium gluconate gel, which is used as an initial response to skin exposure of Hydrofluoric acid. The quantities of Hydrofluoric acid that are used and stored should be kept to an absolute minimum. All users of hydrofluoric acid must attend hydrofluoric acid training. More information on hydrofluoric acid can be found in the Laboratory Safety Manual and Chemical Hygiene Plan. Due to the toxic nature, do not attempt to neutralize hydrofluoric acid - dispose of hydrofluoric acid waste through the hazardous waste management program .
操作步骤：Bench top use of hydrofluoric acid is not permitted; it must only be used in a fume hood.; Anyone using Hydrofluoric acid must contact the Gannett Health Center and purchase a tube of Calcium gluconate gel,...; The quantities of Hydrofluoric acid that are used and stored should be kept to an absolute minimum.; All users of hydrofluoric acid must attend hydrofluoric acid training.; Due to the toxic nature, do not attempt to neutralize hydrofluoric acid - dispose of hydrofluoric acid waste through...; Because of hydrofluoric acid’s ability to etch glass, the chemical and waste must be stored in plastic containers.

Due to the reactive nature, do not attempt to neutralize perchloric acid - dispose of perchloric acid waste through the hazardous waste management program . 7.2 Organic Solvents Most spent organic solvents will be classified as an F-Listed or Characteristic hazardous waste. Laboratories or other areas generating more than 5 gallons of hazardous waste (spent solvents) per month should accumulate the waste in safety cans.

标题：Cornell Hazardous Waste Manual - 7.5 Asbestos
类别：废弃物
子类别：危险废物手册

问题：7.5 Asbestos相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Asbestos is a fibrous material that was once widely used in a number of products that can still be found in laboratories and throughout other buildings. Products that can contain asbestos include: electrical equipment insulation (ovens, heating mantles, heating pads, and wires), older vinyl floor tiles and mastic, pipe fittings, pipe insulation, caulking compounds, fireproofing, and transite (cement-like) panels such as those found in and under fume hoods. Asbestos is a known human carcinogen and must be disposed of properly. The hazard of asbestos is greatest when the asbestos product becomes “friable” – able to be pulverized from finger pressure – and when the asbestos becomes airborne. For older vinyl asbestos tile (VAT), an additional slipping hazard occurs when these tiles “pop” out of the floor. If you find any of the above items deteriorating and suspect they may contain asbestos, or you are considering disposing of old electrical equipment with insulation, or if vinyl tiles have “popped” out of the floor, then please contact the asbestos coordinator at 607-254-5439 for more information.
操作步骤：Asbestos is a known human carcinogen and must be disposed of properly.; If you find any of the above items deteriorating and suspect they may contain asbestos, or you are considering...

废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。

R5 Group is also responsible for managing other recyclable materials such as Used Oil, Scrap Metal, Batteries, Refrigerated Appliances, old Computers, and Electronic Equipment. Used photographic fixer contains Silver above regulatory levels and cannot be poured down the drain; however, some photographic developers and other chemicals may be disposed of down the drain depending on the chemical constituents.

标题：Cornell Hazardous Waste Manual - 7.15 Reactive and Potentially Explosive Chemicals
类别：废弃物
子类别：危险废物手册

适用场景：参考Cornell University EHS公开资料处理危险废物手册相关实验室安全问题
问题：7.15 Reactive and Potentially Explosive Chemicals相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Reactive chemicals such as strong oxidizers and reducers, and air/water reactive chemicals must be disposed of through the hazardous waste management program. Because of their reactive nature, it is important to minimize the quantity of reactive chemicals in storage. If the integrity of the container appears to be compromised, then dispose of the chemicals as hazardous waste promptly. Never dispose of reactive chemicals, such as Sodium metal, regardless of the quantity, down the drain or in the normal trash. Such practices can result in fires, toxic vapors and gases being released, and injury to people. When disposing of these compounds, please note any special hazards on the Hazardous Waste Label . Some of these compounds can become unstable and potentially explosive over time due to contamination with air, water, other material, or when the chemical dries out.
操作步骤：Reactive chemicals such as strong oxidizers and reducers, and air/water reactive chemicals must be disposed of...; If the integrity of the container appears to be compromised, then dispose of the chemicals as hazardous waste promptly.; Never dispose of reactive chemicals, such as Sodium metal, regardless of the quantity, down the drain or in the...; When disposing of these compounds, please note any special hazards on the Hazardous Waste Label .; If you feel that there is an immediate potential hazard, please contact EHS at 607-255-8200 for more assistance.
个人防护：按SDS、风险评估和本单位SOP选择PPE
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：泄漏、火灾或失控释放时优先人员撤离、隔离区域、报警并联系EHS/应急人员。
法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

问题：Trinitro-compounds相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：7.16 Peroxide Forming Chemicals Many commonly used chemicals, organic solvents in particular, can form shock, heat, and friction sensitive peroxides upon exposure to oxygen through concentration, evaporation, and distillation. Compounds that are suspected of having very high peroxide levels because of age, unusual viscosity, discoloration, or crystal formation should be considered extremely dangerous. If you discover a container that meets this description, DO NOT attempt to open or move the container. Make other people working in your area aware of the potential explosion hazard and contact EHS immediately at " askEHS ". You will find extensive information related to peroxide forming chemicals , including a list of peroxide formers , and how to test for peroxides in the Laboratory Safety Manual and Chemical Hygiene Plan .

安全结论：You must make every effort to provide an accurate description of all chemicals that you dispose of through the hazardous waste management program. Without an accurate description, the chemical cannot be handled or disposed of safely. Waste disposal companies will not accept unknown chemical waste without the generator providing a sample analysis which can be very expensive. Many unknown chemicals are generated due to a lack of good housekeeping and good laboratory safety practices. ALL containers used to store chemicals must be labeled. Containers in which the labels are degrading or falling off should be given a new label. There are numerous reference materials with methods and procedures that can be used in identifying unknown chemicals.

知识ID：EXT-CORNELL-HW-MANUAL-056-6430bef7d9
标题：Cornell Hazardous Waste Manual - 7.19.2 Deactivation Procedures
类别：废弃物
子类别：危险废物手册
实验室类型：通用

问题：7.19.2 Deactivation Procedures相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Safe management of ethidium bromide (EtBr) involves both prevention of exposure and proper handling of waste. Because EtBr is a potent mutagen, waste solutions, gels, and contaminated surfaces must be treated as hazardous chemical waste. Modern best practice focuses on adsorption and controlled collection rather than bleach oxidation, which is no longer recommended due to incomplete destruction and formation of chlorinated byproducts. Activated Charcoal Adsorption Aqueous EtBr solutions can be treated using activated charcoal filters, columns, or commercial "tea bag" kits . These methods remove EtBr by adsorption. After treatment, the filtrate may be checked under UV light to confirm the absence of orange fluorescence. If no fluorescence is observed, and if permitted by institutional policy, the filtrate may be disposed of via the sanitary drain.
操作步骤：Because EtBr is a potent mutagen, waste solutions, gels, and contaminated surfaces must be treated as hazardous...; The spent charcoal, filters, or bags must be collected and disposed of as hazardous waste.
个人防护：合适材质手套
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求

安全结论：For dilute EtBr solutions (≤100 µg/mL), Amberlite XAD-16 resin or equivalent adsorption media can be used. The resin captures EtBr and is then disposed of as hazardous chemical waste. This method is sometimes used with filtration cartridges designed for nucleic acid dyes. Surface Decontamination For benchtops or equipment contaminated with EtBr, the preferred method is detergent cleaning and waste capture . Wipe the area thoroughly with a laboratory detergent solution (e.g., Alconox) or activated-charcoal wipes. After cleaning, inspect the surface with a handheld UV lamp (302–312 nm) to confirm no orange fluorescence remains. All wipes, paper towels, gloves, and other cleaning materials used during decontamination must be collected in a labeled container and disposed of as hazardous waste.

问题：9.2 Bulk Drums相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Certain categories of liquid chemicals can be bulked and combined into drums. Examples include flammable solvents, acids, bases, and some types of aqueous waste. Bulking waste (as opposed to lab packing) can result in significant cost savings for the University and ultimately your department. Bulking first involves segregating chemicals according to hazard class . Then a small amount of chemical from each container is mixed in a 1-gallon size container to determine if a reaction occurs. If no reactions occur, then the rest of the chemical is poured into a 30- or 55-gallon drum. Accurately labeling chemicals helps to avoid potential reactions, fires, or explosions when chemicals are bulked.

问题：9.2.1 Solvent Recycling相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Cornell EHS and Animal Health Diagnostic Center Department of Biomedical Sciences have jointly purchased a solvent recycling unit. Reduction of non-halogenated solvent hazardous waste generated in the Histology Department is estimated to be approximately 3 tons annually. The reduced cost of waste disposal annually is approximately $1500.00, while the reduction in annual purchase of new xylene and ethanol is estimated to be just over $8,000.00. The return of investment for this unit should be just over 2 years. The recycling accomplished by Histology is not feasible in all laboratories because of an inability to segregate halogens from non-halogenated solvents. Therefore, the afore-mentioned procedure in section 9.2 is an effective way to reduce costs for solvent disposal. The following solvents should be segregated from other waste chemicals and stored in their own labeled container whenever possible:

问题：Xylene (can have Propar mixed)相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：9.3 Recycling / Reclamation Chemicals such as used oil, free-flowing mercury, and silver from photographic fixer are sent for recycling/reclamation. Photographic fixer is collected and run through a filtration media to collect the silver. Items containing mercury, such as thermometers and manometers are collected and the mercury is removed. It is important to minimize the amount of other material that is mixed in with these items. The addition of chemicals or other solid waste to these items can result in the material being unable to be reclaimed and having to be disposed as hazardous waste instead. 9.4 Ultimate Disposal There are a variety of treatment/destruction methods that environmental companies use after they receive the waste generated on campus. Some wastes (bulk flammable liquid drums) are used as a secondary fuel source at cement kilns.

问题：Appendix B - Disposal of Nonhazardous Laboratory Waste Down The Sanitary Sewer for Ithaca Campus相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Chemical Drain Disposal Research and other operations at Cornell University generate chemical waste requiring disposal. Some of these chemicals can be recycled in the chemical surplus program to be reused by other members of the Cornell community, while other chemicals are classified as hazardous waste and specific rules must be followed, prior to disposal, to be in compliance with federal, state and local regulations. This appendix provides information for compliance with the Ithaca Area Waste Water Treatment Facility (IAWWTF) established requirements and limitations regarding disposal of chemicals into campus laboratory drain systems. Drainage from disposal systems on the core Ithaca campus terminate at the IAWWTF. Limitations may differ for locations that are not connected to the Ithaca area sanitary sewer system (such as laboratories in Geneva, New York City, or other locations) and additional prohibitions will apply to any drain that terminates at a local on-site system (leach field or similar). Do not dispose of any chemicals into a storm sewer or similar untreated disposal options. Contact your local EHS representative for guidance in areas outside of the core Ithaca campus.

标题：Cornell Hazardous Waste Manual - Prohibited From Drain Disposal
类别：废弃物
子类别：危险废物手册

问题：Prohibited From Drain Disposal相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Certain classes of chemicals cannot be poured down the drain - they must be collected, managed and disposed of as hazardous waste using the Cornell University Department of Environmental Health and Safety’s waste procedures. If you have questions regarding the proper collection and disposal of aqueous solutions, low concentrations or small volumes of chemicals within the categories below, contact EHS at " askEHS ". The following classes of chemicals are prohibited from drain disposal: Any flammable liquids with a flashpoint less than 140 degrees F – including but not limited to any quantity of gasoline, kerosene, naptha, benzene, toluene, xylene, fuel oil, ethers, ketones, aldehydes, chlorates, perchlorates, bromates, carbides, hydrides and sulfides. This does not include aqueous solutions of these compounds that have a flashpoint greater than 140 degrees F. Any Liquids, Solids or Gases that pose a fire hazard alone or can potentially interact with other chemicals in the sewer and become a fire or explosion hazard. Solutions outside the pH range of 5.5 to 9.5. Labs may neutralize acids and bases to a pH within this range and then drain dispose, provided there are no prohibited items in the solution.

标题：Cornell Hazardous Waste Manual - Accidental Discharge
类别：废弃物
子类别：危险废物手册
实验室类型：通用

问题：Accidental Discharge相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：The campus sanitary sewer discharge permit issued by IAWWF and sewer use law have reporting requirements for accidental discharge. Anyone causing an accidental discharge of a prohibited material to the sanitary sewer must notify EH&S IMMEDIATELY during normal business hours at 607-255-8200. This includes materials accidently poured or spilled down the drain via sink, floor drain, or plumbed equipment. For accidental discharges from construction or utilities activities, notify EHS IMMEDIATELY at 607-255-8200 during normal business hours. If accidental discharges occur after EHS normal business hours NOTIFY CORNELL DISPATCH AT 607-255-1111. Normal business hours are 8 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Thursday and 8 am to 4 pm Fridays. Faculty, staff and students should be made aware of their roles and responsibilities for accidental discharge by in-house training and or posting in a central communication area.
操作步骤：The campus sanitary sewer discharge permit issued by IAWWF and sewer use law have reporting requirements for...; Anyone causing an accidental discharge of a prohibited material to the sanitary sewer must notify EH&S IMMEDIATELY...; Faculty, staff and students should be made aware of their roles and responsibilities for accidental discharge by in-...
个人防护：按SDS、风险评估和本单位SOP选择PPE
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：如产生废弃物，按SDS、本单位EHS分类和标签要求收集处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。

法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

知识ID：EXT-CORNELL-HW-MANUAL-079-0d02b06f19
标题：Cornell Hazardous Waste Manual - There are some easy ways to preventing the generation of unknown chemicals/materials:
类别：废弃物
子类别：危险废物手册
实验室类型：通用
风险等级：1
危险类型：危险废物;标签;暂存;处置;卫星积累区
适用场景：参考Cornell University EHS公开资料处理危险废物手册相关实验室安全问题
问题：There are some easy ways to preventing the generation of unknown chemicals/materials:相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Ensure that a label is present on all containers of chemicals including containers of wastes. This means all containers even beakers, test tubes, wash bottles and other containers. Use chemical names to identify the contents of containers. For hazardous wastes generated at Cornell this is a requirement. Do not use formulas, abbreviations or chemical structures on waste labels. Containers in which the labels are degrading or falling off should be given a new label immediately. Check laboratory notebooks for information related to vials or test tubes.
操作步骤：Ensure that a label is present on all containers of chemicals including containers of wastes.; Use chemical names to identify the contents of containers.; Do not use formulas, abbreviations or chemical structures on waste labels.; Containers in which the labels are degrading or falling off should be given a new label immediately.; Many researchers in labs keep detailed notes on what was placed in these containers.; If chemical wastes cannot be identified, fill out a Cornell two-part Hazardous Waste Label.
个人防护：按SDS、风险评估和本单位SOP选择PPE
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。
急救措施：发生暴露后立即停止操作，冲洗/脱除污染物并按本单位流程就医和报告。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。

法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

知识ID：EXT-YALE-CHP-020-125caffaa6
标题：Yale Laboratory Chemical Hygiene Plan - INTRODUCTION
类别：化学
子类别：化学卫生计划
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：2
危险类型：化学卫生计划;PPE;通风柜;高危化学品
适用场景：参考Yale Environmental Health & Safety公开资料处理化学卫生计划相关实验室安全问题
问题：INTRODUCTION相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：The Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP) is a requirement for non-production laboratories where chemicals are used in accordance with the Occupational Safety & Health Administration’s (OSHA) Occupational Exposure to Hazardous Chemicals in Laboratories standard (29 CFR 1910.1450), more commonly referred to as the Laboratory Standard. This plan applies to all Yale University faculty, staff, students, and visitors who use hazardous materials in laboratory settings. The CHP does not address the use of radioactive materials or biological agents. Information on these materials is available in the University’s Radiation Safety Manual and Biosafety Manual, respectively. Where additional regulatory standards apply (e.g., CLIA, CAP, Radiation Safety, Biosafety), this Plan supplements those requirements. The most protective standard governs.
操作步骤：This plan applies to all Yale University faculty, staff, students, and visitors who use hazardous materials in...; The CHP does not address the use of radioactive materials or biological agents.
个人防护：必要时呼吸防护
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：如产生废弃物，按SDS、本单位EHS分类和标签要求收集处置。
急救措施：发生暴露后立即停止操作，冲洗/脱除污染物并按本单位流程就医和报告。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。
法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

问题：The standard operating procedures (laboratory practices and engineering controls) recommended in this plan相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：specify the safeguards to be implemented when handling hazardous chemicals. These safeguards will protect laboratory personnel from unsafe conditions in most situations. There are instances, however, when the physical and chemical properties, the proposed use, the quantity used for a particular purpose, or the toxicity of a substance are such that additional or fewer controls may be appropriate to protect the laboratory worker. Professional judgment is essential when interpreting these standard operating procedures, and individual laboratories may modify them to meet their specific uses and operational needs. These modifications and lab-specific SOPs must be maintained by the laboratory and be available for review.
操作步骤：There are instances, however, when the physical and chemical properties, the proposed use, the quantity used for a...; These modifications and lab-specific SOPs must be maintained by the laboratory and be available for review.

废弃物处置：如产生废弃物，按SDS、本单位EHS分类和标签要求收集处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。

Information on Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for specific laboratory tasks is available in the Yale University PPE Assessment Tables/Tools for Laboratories. Every laboratory member should know the locations and proper use of available protective clothing and equipment, as well as emergency equipment/procedures. Additional information on protective clothing and equipment is also contained in SECTION 2.3 PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND LABORATORY SAFETY EQUIPMENT of this manual.

知识ID：EXT-YALE-CHP-041-230696641f
标题：Yale Laboratory Chemical Hygiene Plan - 1.5.2.1 Container Labeling
类别：化学
子类别：化学卫生计划
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：2
危险类型：化学卫生计划;PPE;通风柜;高危化学品
适用场景：参考Yale Environmental Health & Safety公开资料处理化学卫生计划相关实验室安全问题
问题：1.5.2.1 Container Labeling相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：All containers of hazardous chemicals must be labeled identifying their contents. Labels on hazardous chemicals must not be removed or defaced except when empty. Chemical labels on purchased chemicals are required to provide you with safety information to help you protect yourself while working with this substance. This includes physical and health hazard warnings, protective measures for handling the material, first-aid instructions, storage information, and procedures to follow in the event of a fire, leak, or spill. All labels on chemicals purchased after June 2015 must include the information required by the OSHA Hazard Communication Standard. Manufacturers and importers of these chemicals must provide a label that includes a signal word (Danger, Warning), pictogram(s), hazard statement(s), and precautionary statement(s) based on the hazard classification and category of the chemical. This requirement ensures consistent, uniform hazard information across all chemical containers, regardless of manufacturer or supplier.
操作步骤：All containers of hazardous chemicals must be labeled identifying their contents.; Labels on hazardous chemicals must not be removed or defaced except when empty.; Chemical labels on purchased chemicals are required to provide you with safety information to help you protect...; All labels on chemicals purchased after June 2015 must include the information required by the OSHA Hazard...; Manufacturers and importers of these chemicals must provide a label that includes a signal word (Danger, Warning),...; Read the label each time you use a newly purchased chemical.
个人防护：合适材质手套
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：如产生废弃物，按SDS、本单位EHS分类和标签要求收集处置。

问题：1.6 CHEMICAL EXPOSURE ASSESSMENT相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Regular environmental or personal exposure monitoring of airborne concentrations is not usually warranted or practical in laboratories because chemicals are typically used for relatively short periods, in small quantities, and/or within laboratory fume hoods or other local exhaust ventilation systems. Exposure monitoring may be appropriate when a highly toxic substance is used regularly or for an extended period, when hazardous chemicals are used outside a fume hood/local exhaust ventilation, or when quantities are larger than lab-scale. During annual laboratory safety inspections, Safety Advisors from EHS will identify these situations, and Industrial Hygienists from Yale EHS will perform follow-up exposure assessments as necessary.
操作步骤：Regular environmental or personal exposure monitoring of airborne concentrations is not usually warranted or...; Exposure monitoring may be appropriate when a highly toxic substance is used regularly or for an extended period,...; During annual laboratory safety inspections, Safety Advisors from EHS will identify these situations, and Industrial...

Exposure assessments refer to the quantitative evaluation of hazardous materials, i.e., environmental (workplace) monitoring or measurement of toxic substances or harmful physical agents. Occupational medical records include medical questionnaires, results of pre-employment, pre-assignment, periodic, or episodic medical examinations, laboratory tests taken to establish a baseline or detect occupational illness, and associated medical opinions, diagnoses, recommendations, and treatments, as applicable.

问题：2.1.3 Housekeeping相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Keep all aisles, hallways, and stairs clear of all chemicals. Stairways and hallways should not be used for storage. • Keep all work areas, and especially work benches, clear of clutter and obstructions. • All working surfaces should be cleaned regularly. • Access to emergency equipment, utility controls, electrical panels, showers, eyewashes, fire extinguishers, and exits should never be blocked. • Waste must be stored in appropriate containers and be properly labeled. All hazardous waste containers must be labeled with the full chemical names of the contents and the words “hazardous waste”.
操作步骤：Keep all aisles, hallways, and stairs clear of all chemicals.; Stairways and hallways should not be used for storage.; • Keep all work areas, and especially work benches, clear of clutter and obstructions.; • All working surfaces should be cleaned regularly.; • Access to emergency equipment, utility controls, electrical panels, showers, eyewashes, fire extinguishers, and...; • Waste must be stored in appropriate containers and be properly labeled.

废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。

应急升级：泄漏、火灾或失控释放时优先人员撤离、隔离区域、报警并联系EHS/应急人员。

标题：Yale Laboratory Chemical Hygiene Plan - 2.1.4 Glassware Safety
类别：化学
子类别：化学卫生计划

问题：2.1.4 Glassware Safety相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Handle and store laboratory glassware with care. Borosilicate glassware is recommended for all laboratory glassware except for special experiments that use UV or other light sources. Any glass equipment to be evacuated, such as suction flasks, should be specially designed with heavy walls to withstand pressure. Glass equipment in pressure or vacuum service should be provided with shielding to protect users and other laboratory occupants. Glass vessels at reduced pressure can collapse violently, either spontaneously (if cracked or weakened) or from an accidental blow. Use extra care with Dewar flasks and other evacuated glassware; shield or wrap them with safety netting to contain chemicals or fragments in the event of an implosion.
操作步骤：Handle and store laboratory glassware with care.; Borosilicate glassware is recommended for all laboratory glassware except for special experiments that use UV or...; Any glass equipment to be evacuated, such as suction flasks, should be specially designed with heavy walls to...; Glass equipment in pressure or vacuum service should be provided with shielding to protect users and other laboratory...; Use extra care with Dewar flasks and other evacuated glassware; shield or wrap them with safety netting to contain...
个人防护：合适材质手套
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：如产生废弃物，按SDS、本单位EHS分类和标签要求收集处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。

问题：EQUIPMENT相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：2.3.1 Standard Laboratory Clothing – Appropriate Attire Even when there is no immediate risk of skin contact with a hazardous chemical, it is still important to wear clothing that minimizes exposed skin when in the laboratory. Laboratory Personnel must wear safety or prescription glasses, pants or clothing that covers the legs (shorts and short skirts are not acceptable), and closed- toe, solid-top shoes in the laboratory at all times. Safety glasses, exam-style gloves, and a laboratory coat (or its equivalent in certain circumstances – apron, barrier gown, etc.) are required to be worn whenever working with hazardous materials. Prescription glasses may be worn only when working with hazardous materials if they are prescription safety glasses with side shields. Laboratory coats are intended to prevent contact with dirt, chemical dusts, and minor chemical splashes or spills. If a lab coat becomes contaminated, it should be removed immediately, and the affected skin surface thoroughly washed.

知识ID：EXT-YALE-CHP-076-74c9f8ff2a
标题：Yale Laboratory Chemical Hygiene Plan - 2.3.3 Gloves
类别：化学
子类别：化学卫生计划
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：2
危险类型：化学卫生计划;PPE;通风柜;高危化学品
适用场景：参考Yale Environmental Health & Safety公开资料处理化学卫生计划相关实验室安全问题
问题：2.3.3 Gloves相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Chemical-resistant gloves must be worn whenever handling hazardous chemicals or whenever there is a possibility of contact with hazardous materials. Gloves should be selected based on the materials being handled, the specific hazard involved, and the operation's requirements. Before each use, gloves should be checked for integrity. Exam-style gloves are most commonly used for laboratory work and are disposed of in the regular trash after each use. In general, nitrile exam-style gloves provide better chemical protection than latex or vinyl gloves. All laboratories that use chemicals should stock and use nitrile gloves. Latex gloves are discouraged not only because they do not hold up well to many chemicals, but also because of the potential for the user or other lab personnel to develop a sensitization to the latex.
操作步骤：Chemical-resistant gloves must be worn whenever handling hazardous chemicals or whenever there is a possibility of...; Gloves should be selected based on the materials being handled, the specific hazard involved, and the operation's...; Before each use, gloves should be checked for integrity.; Exam-style gloves are most commonly used for laboratory work and are disposed of in the regular trash after each use.; All laboratories that use chemicals should stock and use nitrile gloves.; Nitrile exam-style gloves are generally more chemically resistant than vinyl or latex, but because they are thin, it...
个人防护：合适材质手套
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。
急救措施：发生暴露后立即停止操作，冲洗/脱除污染物并按本单位流程就医和报告。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。
法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

标题：Yale Laboratory Chemical Hygiene Plan - 2.3.4 Eye Protection
类别：化学
子类别：化学卫生计划
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：3
危险类型：化学卫生计划;PPE;通风柜;高危化学品
适用场景：参考Yale Environmental Health & Safety公开资料处理化学卫生计划相关实验室安全问题
问题：2.3.4 Eye Protection相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Eye protection is required for all people present in laboratories where hazardous materials are handled or stored. Prescription eyeglasses may be worn in lieu of safety glasses if not handling hazardous materials in the laboratory, however safety glasses with side shields must be worn when handling hazardous materials. Safety glasses, goggles, and goggles with a face shield should be worn in the laboratory based upon the physical state, the volume, the operation, or the level of toxicity of the chemicals used. Goggles should be worn in situations where bulk quantities of chemicals are handled and chemical splashes to the eyes are possible. Goggles form a liquid-proof seal around the eyes, protecting them from splashes. When handling highly reactive substances, chemicals under pressure, or larger quantities of corrosives, poisons, and hot chemicals, goggles with face shield should be worn.
操作步骤：Eye protection is required for all people present in laboratories where hazardous materials are handled or stored.; Prescription eyeglasses may be worn in lieu of safety glasses if not handling hazardous materials in the laboratory,...; Safety glasses, goggles, and goggles with a face shield should be worn in the laboratory based upon the physical...; Goggles should be worn in situations where bulk quantities of chemicals are handled and chemical splashes to the eyes...; When handling highly reactive substances, chemicals under pressure, or larger quantities of corrosives, poisons, and...
个人防护：护目镜/面屏;合适材质手套

问题：2.3.5 Protection of The Respiratory System相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Inhalation hazards can be best controlled with local exhaust ventilation, such as a laboratory fume hood. Respiratory protection can also be used as a secondary means to protect against inhalation hazards but is not normally required in most laboratories. Check the label and SDS for information on a substance's inhalation hazard and special ventilation requirements. Take appropriate precautions before using these substances. Controlling inhalation exposures through engineering controls (e.g., ventilation) is always the preferred method.

安全结论：ehs.yale.edu/training/laser-safety-training. Laser Registration Requirements: EHS must be notified of the intent to purchase any class 3B or 4 lasers. 问题：Comments相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：ALIGNMENT PROCEDURES Special alignment procedures: Use low power alignment laser, when possible. Use lowest possible energy setting. Survey area (with UV/IR viewer, if necessary) for reflections and confine such reflections to the optics table. Only after completing these procedures should the laser be increased to desired power and repetition rate. If more than one person is present, announce increase in power so that all present are aware of the change.
操作步骤：ALIGNMENT PROCEDURES Special alignment procedures: Use low power alignment laser, when possible.; Use lowest possible energy setting.; Only after completing these procedures should the laser be increased to desired power and repetition rate.

急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。

标题：Yale Laser Standard Operating Procedure - Other tips:
类别：物理

问题：Other tips:相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Allow only trained personnel to be present during alignment. Minimize the number of personnel present during the alignment. All present must wear appropriate eyewear. If possible, avoid using beam paths that are at sitting or standing eye level. Where feasible, use low power (class 2 or 3A) visible lasers to simulate the path of high power or invisible lasers. Where feasible, terminate laser beams and specular reflections on diffuse reflecting beam blocks. Use phosphor cards, IR viewers, video cameras or other display devices to locate invisible beams.
操作步骤：All present must wear appropriate eyewear.; If possible, avoid using beam paths that are at sitting or standing eye level.; Where feasible, use low power (class 2 or 3A) visible lasers to simulate the path of high power or invisible lasers.; Use phosphor cards, IR viewers, video cameras or other display devices to locate invisible beams.; Use beam shutters to block high power beams any time they are not actually needed.

安全结论：Open-toed shoes, short pants, or skirts are also prohibited. Jewelry, including watches, must also be removed before beginning work. Long hair must be tied up and secured (not hanging), or tucked in a hat or hairnet. Long beards must also be contained. Focus on your work and the machine. Cell phones, music players, and other personal electronic devices can be dangerously distracting – do not use them when working at a machine.

应急升级：泄漏、火灾或失控释放时优先人员撤离、隔离区域、报警并联系EHS/应急人员。
法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

知识ID：EXT-MIT-CHEM-HYGIENE-001-ed33cf9dc0
标题：MIT Chemical Hygiene - Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP)
类别：化学
子类别：化学卫生
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：3
危险类型：化学卫生计划;危险化学品;PPE;培训
适用场景：参考MIT Environment, Health & Safety公开资料处理化学卫生相关实验室安全问题
问题：Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP)相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：All MIT Departments, Laboratories, Centers and Institutes (DLCI) that engage in the laboratory use of hazardous chemicals are required to develop and carry out the provisions of a written Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP) that meets the requirements of the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) “Laboratory Standard” and MIT policies and required procedures. CHPs are written documents that establish the administrative measures and standard operating procedures for safely and responsibly using chemical materials in laboratories. Your CHP contains information on how to safely handle corrosives, carcinogens, flammables, toxics, particularly hazardous substances, and other hazardous materials including those with physical hazards. To assist those DLCI that must prepare a CHP, the MIT Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Office has prepared a Chemical Hygiene Plan Template. This template provides a customizable CHP that meets the Institute’s requirements for the use of common laboratory chemicals and procedures. The Template also provides assistance in the development of specialized standard operating procedures to accommodate the unique materials and procedures in specific laboratories.
操作步骤：All MIT Departments, Laboratories, Centers and Institutes (DLCI) that engage in the laboratory use of hazardous...; Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) “Laboratory Standard” and MIT policies and required procedures.; To assist those DLCI that must prepare a CHP, the MIT Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Office has prepared a...; This template provides a customizable CHP that meets the Institute’s requirements for the use of common laboratory...; Laboratory Users of Hazardous Chemicals Every user of hazardous chemicals at MIT must be trained to handle them safely.; To ensure this, all students and employees in the department who use hazardous chemicals in a laboratory must read...
个人防护：合适材质手套
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：如产生废弃物，按SDS、本单位EHS分类和标签要求收集处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。
法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

问题：General waste management practices相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：All faculty, students, and staff who generate hazardous waste must complete the “Chemical Safety for Laboratories” training course (EHS-1900). Read more about the Chemical Waste Pickup services. Access the online hazardous Waste Tag system. All lab wastes containing chemical constituents are presumed by the State of California to be regulated hazardous wastes. If, due to your own knowledge and experience, you believe your waste may be non-hazardous, but it is not on the list, contact EH&S for a waste determination. Reagent chemical containers that are in good condition and have a readable original manufacturer’s label are considered surplus chemicals. Lab personnel must affix a surplus sticker before requesting pickup by EH&S, but do not need a hazardous waste tag.

问题：Report an Incident (SU-17)相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Health & Safety Topics Standard Operating Procedures Biohazardous waste includes all laboratory waste that may contain any biohazardous material or were in contact with said material. Additionally, any blood or components of blood or body fluids are to be disposed of as biohazardous waste, as are human or non-human primate cell lines. All biohazardous waste must be disposed of in red bags marked with the biohazard symbol; these bags must be secondarily contained in a puncture resistant outer container and covered with a tight fitting lid. Biohazard stickers must be present on all four sides of the container and the top of the lid. In accordance with the California Medical Waste Management Act, Health and Safety Code, Chapter 6.1, medical waste is defined as including, but not limited to the following: Human or animal specimens or cultures from medical and pathological laboratories. Cultures and stocks of infectious agents from research and industrial laboratories. Wastes from the production of bacteria, viruses, or the use of spores, discarded live and attenuated vaccines, and culture dishes and devices used to transfer, inoculate, and mix cultures.

类别：化学

问题：Standard operating procedures (SOPs)相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：A standard operating procedure are step-by-step instructions to help personnel perform specific tasks and work processes, ensuring consistent quality and compliance with safety standards and best practices. If you operate a chemical laboratory, you must have standard operating procedures (SOPs) that describe the safety measures for using, storing, and disposing of chemicals in your lab. Visit the Chemical SOPs page for templates and a list of required elements you can refer to when developing your SOPs. Environmental Health & Safety provides the following resources for University personnel working in areas where chemicals are present. If you transfer a chemical into a secondary container, it must be labeled correctly to ensure workers are aware of its contents and hazards associated with the chemicals. Be prepared to respond to an exposure or other emergency. A fume hood (or biosafety cabinet) is used when working with toxic compounds to prevent exposure to chemical fumes.
操作步骤：If you operate a chemical laboratory, you must have standard operating procedures (SOPs) that describe the safety...; Visit the Chemical SOPs page for templates and a list of required elements you can refer to when developing your SOPs.; If you transfer a chemical into a secondary container, it must be labeled correctly to ensure workers are aware of...; Use MyChem to record and update your chemical inventory, exchange chemicals with other users, and download the safety...; Determine the required and recommended personal protective equipment.; Safety dispose of chemical waste by requesting a chemical waste collection.
个人防护：按SDS、风险评估和本单位SOP选择PPE
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。
急救措施：发生暴露后立即停止操作，冲洗/脱除污染物并按本单位流程就医和报告。
应急升级：泄漏、火灾或失控释放时优先人员撤离、隔离区域、报警并联系EHS/应急人员。
法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

类别：废弃物

问题：Manage chemical waste safely相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：University personnel who generate hazardous chemical waste at the University (including all campuses and off-site locations) are required to follow chemical waste management practices. Refer to the UW Laboratory Safety Manual for additional information. EH&S recommends hazardous chemical waste generators use the Hazardous Waste Checklist as a self-audit tool to verify compliance with waste accumulation rules and prepare for periodic hazardous waste inspections by the Washington State Department of Ecology. Chemical waste basics What is “hazardous chemical waste”? Hazardous chemical waste is defined as any liquid, gaseous, or solid chemical that is ignitable, corrosive, reactive, toxic, or persistent, and is no longer useful or wanted. Some additional chemicals are managed as hazardous waste at UW because they are known, probable or suspected carcinogens, teratogens, irritants and/or sensitizers (refer to a chemical’s safety data sheet to determine if the chemical is any of these.) Mixtures of chemicals may not be hazardous waste, depending on their concentration and toxicity. Refer to Section 3 of the Laboratory Safety Manual for information on how to calculate whether a mixture of chemicals is hazardous waste.

废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。
急救措施：发生暴露后立即停止操作，冲洗/脱除污染物并按本单位流程就医和报告。

问题：Frequently asked questions相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Why do I need to submit a Chemical Waste Collection Request before EH&S picks up my chemical waste? EH&S needs the information you provide in the Chemical Waste Collection Request for safety, legal, and logistical reasons. Safety: Knowing the potential hazards associated with each container allows EH&S staff to prepare for safely evaluating, handling, transporting, and storing chemicals prior to disposal. Environmental Protection Agency, U.S. Department of Transportation, and Washington State Department of Ecology regulations require us to accurately designate the contents of each container so it can be transported legally and disposed of properly by applying the correct hazardous waste codes and treatment standards. Logistical: We need to know in advance what’s inside the containers to be sure we don’t pick up anything that can’t be transported or disposed of. We also need to know how many containers there are, and the type(s) and size(s) of containers to ensure we have the correct number of transport tubs and space in the vehicle.

Get rid of unused chemicals before they become “waste-like.” Waste-like chemicals are items with faded labels, deteriorating containers, leaks and/or other obvious signs that the chemicals are not being used. 安全结论：Do I need to autoclave micropipet tips that were used for PCR? Because recombinant or synthetic DNA/RNA is considered a biohazard, those tips do need to be autoclaved. Also, if your lab does any biohazardous work, it is easier to treat all pipets and tips as biohazardous so that you do not have to make a decision for each tip; instead, they all go as biohazardous waste. Can EH&S pick up my sharps container or biohazardous waste? EH&S does not collect or treat sharps or other biohazardous waste. EH&S provides consultation and training for on-site or off-site treatment of sharps and biohazardous waste prior to disposal. Check with your department to see if a sharps disposal waste stream already exists.

问题：Shipping Hazardous Materials相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Treatment and Recycling Notice of Cleaning and Decontamination Fume hoods are a primary method of exposure control in the laboratory. A fume hood is a ventilated enclosure that usually vents separately from the building’s heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) system and not recirculated into the building. Fume hoods should be used when working with toxic compounds or compounds with a boiling point below 120°C. Fume hoods, or other effective local ventilation, must be provided and used when the materials used will exceed exposure limits in the laboratory.

问题：American Industrial Hygiene Association Workplace Environmental Exposure Limits (AIHA WEELs)相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Types of fume hoods at the University include chemical, radioisotope and perchloric acid hoods, with various airflow controls. Fume hood controls include constant air volume (CAV), variable air volume (VAV) and two-state (two speed) control. A number of older wood fume hoods and fume “cupboards” are still maintained. The hoods will display a label that identifies what type of ventilation control is employed: Fume hoods are categorized into one of two groups: 1) standard flow, and 2) low flow. Standard flow fume hoods are designed to operate at 100 linear feet per minute (LFM) at 18 inches sash height. (Note that some legacy hoods were designed to operate at 100 LFM at full sash height, as high as 25 inches). Low flow fume hoods are designed to operate at 70 LFM at 18 inches sash height.

问题：Fume hood testing and inspection相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：EH&S performs a functional performance test to assure hoods perform as required about every 18 months. The performance test typically includes an evaluation of the face velocity, the sound, containment, monitor performance and the tracking ability of a VAV (when applicable). EH&S may also note any observed problem with controls, sash, baffles, plumbing, light or corrosion. Fume hoods tested by EH&S will have a label that records its inspection history: The following definitions are used by EH&S to track the operational status of fume hoods. If a hood fails an inspection, it may need to be taken out of service until repaired. EH&S will notify the researchers and post a “Do Not Use” sign if repair is required. When UW Facilities has completed repairs, EH&S will retest the hood and put it back in service.

标题：UW Fume Hoods Use Inspection and Maintenance - What you need to know
类别：化学

问题：What you need to know相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Use your fume hood, or other engineering controls, rather than the benchtop when there is a possibility of overexposure to air contaminants generated by a laboratory activity. In the event of lab move out and some services/repairs, lab personnel and researchers are responsible for decontamination of their fume hoods. Complete and post this form when performing fume hood decontamination (UW Form 1803: Notice of Laboratory Equipment Decontamination). Be aware of ventilation system shutdowns and do not use the hood when the ventilation system serving the room is shut down. Most fume hoods are equipped with monitors that will generate an audible and, in some cases, a visible alarm when the airflow drops to approximately 80% of the design velocity. The following guidelines should be followed if your alarm activates: Be certain you are operating the hood at or below the sash arrows. If the alarm persists, close the sash and wait a moment and then reopen the sash to your working height.

问题：Frequently asked questions相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Is my fume hood a perchloric acid hood? Procedures using concentrated perchloric acid (>70%) or heat any amount or concentration of perchloric acid must be performed in a closed system or within a specially designed perchloric acid fume hood with wash down systems to prevent the accumulation of explosive perchlorates in the hood and ducting. Perchloric acid hoods shall be prominently labeled “Perchloric Acid Hood.” For assistance in purchasing or locating a perchloric acid fume hood, contact EH&S. Can I use my fume hood during ventilation shutdowns? Laboratories can experience ventilation shutdowns. These shutdowns can be the result of planned maintenance work as well as unplanned events such as equipment failure or power outages. Do not use fume hoods when the ventilation system serving a room is not functioning.

问题：Cal/OSHA Fume Hood definition:相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：A device enclosed except for necessary exhaust purposes on three sides and top and bottom, designed to draw air inward by means of mechanical ventilation, operated with insertion of only the hands and arms of the user, and used to control exposure to hazardous substances. These devices are also known as laboratory fume hoods. Chemical fume hoods, when used properly, are one of the most reliable engineering controls in the laboratory. They protect workers by: Containing vapors, dusts, gases, and fumes generated within the hood, and removing them as air flows into the hood and then out via the laboratory exhaust system

知识ID：EXT-UCSD-FUME-HOODS-004-173524b2d6
标题：UC San Diego Chemical Fume Hoods Overview - Constant air volume hoods
类别：化学
子类别：通风柜
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：2
危险类型：通风柜;排风;操作规范;工程控制
适用场景：参考UC San Diego Blink公开资料处理通风柜相关实验室安全问题
问题：Constant air volume hoods相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：The constant air volume (CAV) fume hood exhausts the same amount of air all the time, regardless of sash position. As the sash is lowered and raised, the velocity at the face of the hood changes. EH&S tests all hoods regularly and marks the opening that gives the correct face velocity (see image at left) on constant air volume hoods. Variable air volume hoods Some newer models, called variable air volume (VAV) hoods, modulate air flow based on sash height and maintain 100 feet per minute face velocity at all sash heights. EH&S tests VAV hoods, but does not mark the sash height since it's always 100 feet per minute. VAV fume hoods are equipped with a monitor (see image at right) that indicates whether the hood is in "standard operation" or "standby operation" mode. The fume hood monitor also has an "emergency purge" button, which increases airflow through the hood to maximum and can be used to quickly remove air contaminates from the lab.
操作步骤：Contact Facilities Management, (858) 534-2930, if your fume hood alarm sounds.
个人防护：按SDS、风险评估和本单位SOP选择PPE
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：如产生废弃物，按SDS、本单位EHS分类和标签要求收集处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：泄漏、火灾或失控释放时优先人员撤离、隔离区域、报警并联系EHS/应急人员。
法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

标题：UC San Diego Chemical Fume Hoods Overview - Biohazardous materials
类别：化学

问题：Biohazardous materials相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Fume hoods are not for use with biohazardous materials. Use a biological safety cabinet, (BSC), for work with infectious agents. BSCs are designed to protect the worker and the environment from biological agents, and to protect the research materials from contamination. Highly toxic materials In some cases, for highly toxic materials a glove box or another containment device is preferred over a chemical fume hood. Contact Environment, Health & Safety (EH&S) for guidance on containment needs. Ductless fume hoods are not allowed at UC San Diego as per UC San Diego Policy and the University of California Lab Safety Design Manual. UCSD's chemical fume hoods are inspected and tested annually by EH&S for functionality and condition.
操作步骤：Fume hoods are not for use with biohazardous materials.; Use a biological safety cabinet, (BSC), for work with infectious agents.; Contact Environment, Health & Safety (EH&S) for guidance on containment needs.

急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。

问题：Select compatible containers相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Chemical compatibility: Choose a container chemically compatible with the material it will hold. Chemicals must not react with, weaken, or dissolve the container or lid. Follow these basic compatibility guidelines: Acids or bases: Do not store in metal. Hydrofluoric acid: Do not store in glass. Gasoline (solvents): Do not store or transport in lightweight polyethylene containers such as milk jugs. Read Chemical Compatibility Guidelines for more detailed information. Use waste containers with leak-proof, screw-on caps so contents can't leak if a container tips over.

知识ID：EXT-UCSD-EXTREME-WASTE-012-69ed67b1e8
标题：UC San Diego Extremely Hazardous Chemical Waste - Tag every waste container
类别：废弃物
子类别：极高危化学废物
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：1
危险类型：极高危废物;标签;处置;暂存
适用场景：参考UC San Diego Blink公开资料处理极高危化学废物相关实验室安全问题
问题：Tag every waste container相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Attach a completed hazardous waste tag to the container before you begin using the container to accumulate and store waste. Cross out all other labels on the container. Do not obliterate the original product label; waste technicians need to see what the container held before it was designated as a waste receptacle. Do not overfill liquid waste containers. Leave a sizable amount of head space in the container to allow for expansion and safe transportation — 10% head space is a good rule of thumb. Do not mix solids with liquid waste. Containers found to contain solids during processing by EH&S hazardous waste technicians will be returned to the generator for separation.
操作步骤：Attach a completed hazardous waste tag to the container before you begin using the container to accumulate and store...; Do not obliterate the original product label; waste technicians need to see what the container held before it was...
个人防护：按SDS、风险评估和本单位SOP选择PPE
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：异常、泄漏、设备失效或失控反应时立即升级给PI、实验室负责人和EHS。

This fume hood should be used for Beta and Gamma radiation, with an interior of type 304 stainless steel and seamless welding for easy decontainmation and cleaning. No horizontal sashes should be on these types of fume hoods. Types that require special permission: These fume hoods are limited across UT Austin campuses.

This information can be located on the safety green sticker at the top corner of the fume hood. 问题：I. Identifying Regulated Chemical Wastes相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：A regulated chemical waste is defined as a waste which, due to its quantity, concentration, or physical and chemical characteristics may: cause, or significantly contribute to, an increase in mortality or an increase in serious or incapacitating illness; or pose a substantial present or potential threat to human health or the environment when improperly treated, stored, transported, disposed of, or otherwise managed. Characteristics of Chemical Wastes In the Code of Federal Regulations (40 CFR), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) defines the four fundamental characteristics of regulated waste as: 1. Ignitability - Ignitable materials are defined as materials exhibiting one or more of the following characteristics: Liquids that have a flash point less than 60°C (140°F). Materials other than liquids that are capable, under standard temperature and pressure, of causing fire by friction, adsorption of moisture, or spontaneous chemical changes and, when ignited, burn so vigorously and persistently that they create a hazard. Flammable compressed gases, including those that form flammable mixtures with air. Oxidizers that stimulate combustion of organic materials. Corrosivity - Corrosive materials are defined as materials meeting one or more of the following criteria: Aqueous solutions with a pH of less than or equal to 2 or greater than or equal to 12.5.

废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。

标题：UT Austin Chemical Waste - Separating incompatible waste streams by means of a partition, wall or other device
类别：废弃物
子类别：化学废物

问题：Separating incompatible waste streams by means of a partition, wall or other device相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Inspecting waste containers at least weekly to ensure they are in good condition and not leaking Filling to a safe level (minimum of 1 inch from the opening of the container or 90% of the containers capacity If a container holding hazardous waste is no longer in good condition or if it begins to leak, the generator must transfer the waste from this container to a container that is in good condition, over-pack the container, or manage the waste in some other way that prevents a potential for a release or contamination. Please contact EHS – HMM, (512) 471-3511, if assistance is required.

问题：E. Unknown Chemical Wastes相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：All waste generators and chemical users are responsible for knowing the contents of all containers in their work areas. This includes properly labeling all waste containers and requesting their removal in a timely manner to avoid the generation of unknown wastes. If you have an unknown chemical waste that needs to be removed you should: Try to identify the contents by asking other researchers, shop personnel, building manager or users in your work area if they know who produced the waste If you cannot find the original generator, attempt to narrow down the potential sources of generation If you have exhausted all available information and still cannot identify the waste you may submit as an “Unknown.” EHS – HMM will inspect and analyze the material. EHS – HMM, pays for a Reactive Specialist to categorize unknown waste generated by The University at least every 75-days. Generators of unknown wastes MAY BE responsible for the costs associated with analyzing and disposal of unknown wastes. Unknown wastes require special handling procedures and may not be acceptable for standard removal depending on the container’s condition, source, and other factors.

标题：UT Austin Chemical Waste - F. Peroxide Formers and Other Unstable Chemical Waste
类别：废弃物
子类别：化学废物

问题：F. Peroxide Formers and Other Unstable Chemical Waste相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Disposal and Testing Guidance Older containers of peroxidizable chemicals, or containers of unknown age or history, must be handled very carefully and should never be opened by researchers. Any peroxidizable chemical with visible discoloration, cloudiness, crystallization, wisp-like structures, or oily layer (or other liquid heterogeneity/stratification) should be treated as potentially explosive. Older steel containers that have visible rust may also be extremely dangerous. If any of these conditions are observed on a peroxidizable chemical, or if the origin and age of the container are unknown, do not attempt to move or open the container. If any of such containers are found, please contact EHS – HMM immediately. Testing strips are available from EHS for instances in which laboratories do not have their own peroxide test strips. For peroxides concentrations of < 20 ppm, either neutralize the peroxides in the compounds using an approved method or dispose of the chemical through EHS – HMM and indicate the peroxide level in the notes.

Users need to understand the proper use and limitations of the fume hood. Each fume hood should be equipped with a flow monitor/ alarm. When the alarm sounds, stop work immediately, close the sash, and report the event to facilities liaison. Local exhaust devices other than fume hoods including snorkels and enclosures are also utilized in laboratories for limited applications. Using or modifying these devices for exposure control or exhausting equipment requires EH&S evaluation, review, and approval. EH&S performs annual fume hood inspections and issues work orders on the behalf of the PI when deficiencies are found.

适用场景：参考NC State Environmental Health and Safety公开资料处理实验室安全与安保指南相关实验室安全问题
问题：Visitors (those without key access) must be escorted at all times相关的实验室安全要求是什么？
安全结论：Access for student, visiting scientists, etc is permitted only when regular employees are present (grad students may be considered employees). Access for cleaning, maintenance and repairs should be limited to hours when regular employees are present. Chemicals that are consumed in process, disposed, or shipped should be removed from lab inventory logs when not to be replenished. Particular attention to this inventory reconciliation should be paid to select agents and other highly toxic materials for which individual containers should be accounted for. Certain highly toxic materials should be stored in locked cabinets, freezers, or refrigerators. This applies to sodium cyanide, potassium cyanide, arsenic compounds, select agents, and other materials which may be readily recognizable as poisons.. Emergency plans must be in place.
操作步骤：Access for cleaning, maintenance and repairs should be limited to hours when regular employees are present.; Chemicals that are consumed in process, disposed, or shipped should be removed from lab inventory logs when not to be...; Particular attention to this inventory reconciliation should be paid to select agents and other highly toxic...; Certain highly toxic materials should be stored in locked cabinets, freezers, or refrigerators.; Emergency plans must be in place.; Plans for secured areas should include means for emergency responders to gain access to the work area in the event of...
个人防护：按SDS、风险评估和本单位SOP选择PPE
禁止事项：禁止绕过工程控制、PPE、培训和审批要求
废弃物处置：按危险废物/生物废物/锐器废物类别、标签和容器要求收集，交由本单位合规流程处置。
急救措施：发生人员暴露或不适时立即停止操作、撤离风险源并联系导师/EHS/医疗支持。
应急升级：泄漏、火灾或失控释放时优先人员撤离、隔离区域、报警并联系EHS/应急人员。
法规与制度提示：公开权威资料整理，落地执行时需结合本单位SOP、SDS、EHS审批和适用法规。

Waste generated within a laboratory is regulated by Subpart K and managed under the Laboratory Waste Management Plan (pdf). Non-laboratory areas will manage their waste under the Hazardous Waste Generator Improvements Rule.

知识ID：KB-GAP-8001
标题：使用恒温培养箱时有哪些安全注意事项？
类别：恒温培养箱
子类别：加热设备
实验室类型：化学/生物
风险等级：2
危险类型：过热;火灾;微生物污染
适用场景：恒温培养箱的安全操作
问题：恒温培养箱用于细胞/微生物培养和恒温实验。安全要求：1) 确认温控器准确（用独立温度计校验）；2) 培养箱内不放易燃溶剂或挥发性化学品；3) 定期清洁消毒内壁（防止微生物滋生）；4) CO₂培养箱需定期检查CO₂浓度传感器和管路；5) 培养箱运行时不可频繁开门（温度波动影响实验且浪费能源）；6) 放入的样品需标注日期、内容和责任人。
操作步骤：检查温控器→清洁内壁→放入样品并记录→设定温度→运行时减少开门→定期校验温度
个人防护：手套（取出高温样品时）
禁止事项：禁止在培养箱内存放食品;禁止放入易燃/挥发性化学品;禁止超温运行;禁止不贴标签的样品
废弃物处置：废弃培养物按生物危废处理（需灭活后出实验室）

标题：使用恒温摇床时需要注意什么？
类别：恒温摇床

知识ID：KB-GAP-8003
标题：沙浴和油浴比水浴温度更高（可达300°C+），需要注意什么？
类别：沙浴/油浴安全使用
子类别：加热设备
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：3
危险类型：高温烫伤;油雾;火灾
适用场景：沙浴和油浴加热的安全使用
问题：沙浴和油浴用于>100°C的加热。硅油浴安全要求：1) 硅油浴温度不超过油的闪点（一般不超过250°C）；2) 油浴中必须放置温度计实时监控；3) 硅油长期高温使用会劣化（颜色变深、粘度增加），需定期更换；4) 沙浴可达更高温度但温控较差；5) 加热结束后在油浴旁标注「高温」警示；6) 严禁用水浴替代油浴/沙浴进行高温加热。
操作步骤：确认加热介质适用温度→放入温度计→缓慢升温→实验过程中监控温度→冷却后再取出容器→标注高温警示
个人防护：隔热手套;护目镜;实验服
禁止事项：禁止油浴超闪点使用;禁止湿手或将水溅入高温油浴（剧烈飞溅）;禁止油浴中加热密封容器;禁止没有温度计的情况下加热
废弃物处置：废旧硅油按化学废液处理
急救措施：烫伤：立即用冷水冲洗冷却，就医
应急升级：油浴冒烟/起火：立即断电，用灭火毯覆盖或使用干粉灭火器
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Laboratory Safety Manual Ch.16
来源机构：Cornell EHS
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/chemical-safety/laboratory-safety-manual
标签：油浴;沙浴;高温加热;SOP
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8004
标题：使用Schlenk line进行无水无氧操作时需要注意什么？
类别：Schlenk线安全操作
子类别：真空/惰性气体设备
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：5
危险类型：无水无氧操作;自燃;爆炸;高压气体
适用场景：Schlenk line（双排管）的安全操作
问题：Schlenk line是空气敏感化学的核心设备。安全操作极为重要：1) 使用前检查所有接头、橡胶管、玻璃活栓是否完好；2) 确认真空泵油洁净（受污染泵油可能反应爆炸）；3) 惰性气体（N₂/Ar）减压阀设置正确（出口压力0.1-0.3 bar）；4) 切换真空/惰气时缓慢操作玻璃活栓（过猛可能导致玻璃断裂）；5) 冷阱中必须使用液氮（不是干冰），冷阱在Schlenk line与真空泵之间捕获挥发性溶剂；6) 冷阱在停止真空后不可立即取下——必须先释放真空再断开；7) Schlenk line不可用于处理自燃试剂（如叔丁基锂），此类操作须在手套箱中。
操作步骤：检查管路和活栓→确认泵油状态→设置惰气减压阀→开启真空泵→冷却冷阱→缓慢操作活栓切换→监控压力表→使用后按顺序关闭→清洁冷阱
个人防护：护目镜;实验服;防低温手套（加液氮时）
禁止事项：禁止在Schlenk line上处理自燃试剂;禁止使用有裂纹的玻璃活栓;禁止冷阱未冷却时蒸发大量溶剂;禁止快速切换活栓;禁止未释放真空拆卸冷阱
废弃物处置：冷阱中收集的溶剂按有机废液处理
急救措施：液氮冻伤：温水复温;玻璃割伤：止血清洁就医
应急升级：Schlenk line破裂/泄漏：立即关闭气瓶阀门，停止真空泵，疏散至通风处
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Laboratory Safety Manual Ch.7; Prudent Practices in the Laboratory
来源机构：Cornell EHS / National Academies Press
来源链接：https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK55873/
标签：Schlenk line;无水无氧;双排管;SOP
语言：zh-CN

标题：使用ICP-OES时需要注意哪些安全事项？
类别：电感耦合等离子体发射光谱仪(ICP-OES)安全
子类别：分析仪器
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：4
危险类型：高温等离子体;有毒气体;高压电;紫外辐射
适用场景：ICP-OES的安全操作

禁止事项：禁止等离子体运行时打开炬室门;禁止直视等离子体（紫外伤害眼睛）;禁止氩气耗尽时继续运行;禁止用含HF的样品直接进样（需使用耐HF进样系统）
废弃物处置：含重金属测试废液按重金属危废收集

类别：气质联用仪(GC-MS)安全

标题：使用索氏提取器时要注意哪些安全事项？
类别：索氏提取器安全使用
子类别：样品前处理
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：3
危险类型：易燃溶剂;玻璃破损;长时间加热
适用场景：索氏提取器的安全操作
问题：索氏提取器用于固液连续萃取，通常使用有机溶剂，操作时间可长达数小时。安全要求：1) 所有玻璃接口严密配合（使用适量真空脂），防止溶剂蒸气泄漏；2) 冷凝水在加热前开启，确认水流畅通；3) 加热温度控制在溶剂沸点以上10-20°C（使溶剂蒸气能上升但不过快）；4) 提取过程不可无人值守——溶剂蒸干会导致烧瓶干烧破裂；5) 提取结束后先停加热，继续通冷凝水至装置冷却；6) 使用易燃溶剂时（乙醚、石油醚等）水浴加热（不可用电热套）。
操作步骤：检查玻璃器皿完好→装样品→连接装置→开冷凝水→水浴加热→监控回流速率→结束后先停热→冷却后拆卸→清洗
个人防护：护目镜;实验服;手套
禁止事项：禁止电热套加热易燃溶剂;禁止无人值守时运行;禁止冷凝水中断时继续加热;禁止溶剂蒸干
废弃物处置：提取残液按有机废液处理

标签：索氏提取;固液萃取;SOP

知识ID：KB-GAP-8009
标题：使用超声波细胞破碎仪时需要注意什么？
类别：超声波细胞破碎仪安全
子类别：样品制备
实验室类型：生物/化学
风险等级：3
危险类型：高强度噪声;气溶胶;样品飞溅;探头过热
适用场景：超声波细胞破碎仪的安全使用
问题：超声波细胞破碎仪（探头式超声）输出能量密度远高于超声波清洗器。安全要求：1) 必须佩戴听力防护（耳塞或耳罩）——输出噪声可达100+ dB；2) 探头浸入液面以下足够深度（通常1-2cm）再启动，防止液体飞溅；3) 使用脉冲模式（如5秒开5秒关）避免样品过热；4) 处理生物样本时在生物安全柜内操作（防止气溶胶扩散）；5) 探头为钛合金材质，长期使用会磨损变短（尖端能量密度下降），需定期检查更换。
操作步骤：佩戴听力防护→安装变幅杆→将探头浸入样品→设置功率和脉冲参数→启动→定时检查→结束后清洁探头
个人防护：耳塞/耳罩;护目镜;实验服;手套
禁止事项：禁止空载运行（无液体时启动会损坏探头和变幅杆）;禁止探头接触容器壁;禁止超功率/超时间连续运行;禁止探头未完全停止就取出
废弃物处置：处理后样品按相应类别处置
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Laboratory Safety Manual Ch.16; NIH Lab Safety Guidelines
来源机构：Cornell EHS / NIH
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/chemical-safety/laboratory-safety-manual
标签：超声破碎;细胞破碎;噪声防护;SOP
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8010
标题：使用冻干机冷冻干燥样品时需要遵守什么安全规程？
类别：冻干机(冷冻干燥机)安全操作详解
子类别：样品制备
实验室类型：生物/化学
风险等级：3
危险类型：真空;低温冻伤;玻璃内爆;化学品暴露
适用场景：冻干机的详细安全操作
问题：冻干机通过升华去除样品中的水分。详细安全规程：1) 样品必须完全冷冻（-40°C或更低）后方可开始抽真空（未冻结的样品在真空下会暴沸）；2) 冷阱温度必须低于-50°C（通常-80°C至-105°C）；3) 含有机溶剂的样品必须先挥发掉大部分有机溶剂（用旋蒸或氮吹），残留量过高会损坏真空泵和冷阱；4) 含盐或腐蚀性的样品需特殊处理（可能腐蚀冷阱）；5) 使用厚壁玻璃容器（耐真空），检查有无裂纹；6) 冻干结束先释放真空再关冷阱。
操作步骤：预冻样品至完全凝固→检查冷阱温度→安装样品→关闭排水阀→开启真空泵→监控真空度→结束释放真空→取出样品→化冰清洁
个人防护：防低温手套;护目镜;实验服
禁止事项：禁止冻干未完全凝固的样品;禁止冻干含大量有机溶剂的样品;禁止使用薄壁/有裂纹的玻璃容器;禁止在真空状态下直接断电
废弃物处置：冻干残渣按相应类别处理
急救措施：冻伤：温水复温;玻璃内爆：止血清洁就医
应急升级：玻璃容器内爆：隔离区域，清理碎片;真空泵异常：停机报告维修
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Laboratory Safety Manual Ch.16
来源机构：Cornell EHS
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/chemical-safety/laboratory-safety-manual
标签：冻干机;冷冻干燥;真空;SOP
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8011
标题：手套箱的详细安全操作规程是什么？
类别：手套箱操作详解
子类别：惰性气氛设备
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：5
危险类型：自燃;缺氧;压力;化学品暴露
适用场景：手套箱的详细安全操作规程
问题：手套箱是最复杂的实验室设备之一。详细规程：1) 进出手套箱的物品须通过过渡仓（大仓至少3次抽真空-充惰气循环，小仓至少5次）;2) 禁止带入：水溶液、挥发溶剂、尖锐物品（刺破手套）、含活性氢的溶剂（醇/酸会毒化催化剂）;3) 手套箱内不存放超过日常用量的化学品和溶剂;4) 循环系统定期再生（铜催化剂约每3-6个月再生一次，分子筛约每月）;5) 氧/水含量超标时（H₂O>5ppm或O₂>5ppm），立即停止敏感实验，排查漏点;6) 手套破损须立即停止使用并用胶塞堵住破口，更换手套后重新置换箱内气氛。
操作步骤：检查O₂/H₂O水平→过渡仓净化物品→移入箱内→在箱内操作→清理废物→过渡仓移出物品→记录使用情况
个人防护：护目镜;实验服;箱内手套
禁止事项：禁止带入水/醇/酸;禁止在手套箱内使用针头（刺破手套风险）;禁止在手套破损时继续操作敏感试剂;禁止过载存放;禁止在过渡仓净化未完成时打开内门
废弃物处置：手套箱内产生的废物（手套、纸巾、废溶剂瓶）密封后移出按危废处理
应急升级：手套箱泄漏或手套破损：立即停止敏感操作，排查问题
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Laboratory Safety Manual Ch.2; Prudent Practices
来源机构：Cornell EHS / National Academies Press
来源链接：https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK55873/
标签：手套箱;惰性气氛;无水无氧;SOP
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8012
标题：使用电化学工作站时需要注意什么？
类别：电化学工作站安全
子类别：分析仪器
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：2
危险类型：触电;化学品泄漏;有毒气体
适用场景：电化学工作站的安全操作
问题：电化学工作站涉及电极、电解液和电位控制。安全要求：1) 使用前检查电极线和工作电极/参比电极/对电极连接正确；2) 电解液不得渗漏到电极夹和仪器接口；3) 电解过程中可能产生气体（如电解水产生H₂和O₂），良好通风防止气体积聚；4) 使用有机电解液时在通风柜内操作（如乙腈+四丁基铵盐体系）；5) 参比电极的填充液定期补充（如Ag/AgCl电极的饱和KCl溶液）。
操作步骤：检查电极和连接→安装电解池→添加电解液→设置实验参数→运行测量→结束后取出电极清洗→关机
个人防护：护目镜;实验服;手套
禁止事项：禁止电极连接错误（短路损坏仪器）;禁止电解液泄漏入仪器;禁止在密闭空间长时间电解（气体积聚风险）
废弃物处置：含重金属或有机电解液的废液分类收集

来源标题：Cornell Laboratory Safety Manual Ch.16
来源机构：Cornell EHS
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/chemical-safety/laboratory-safety-manual
标签：电化学工作站;电解;电极;SOP

知识ID：KB-GAP-8013
标题：丁腈手套不能防哪些化学品？使用中有什么限制？
类别：丁腈手套使用限制与注意事项
子类别：手套安全
实验室类型：通用
风险等级：2
危险类型：化学品渗透;手套降解;过敏
适用场景：丁腈手套的使用限制
问题：丁腈手套是实验室最通用的防化手套，但有重要使用限制。不耐受的化学品包括：二氯甲烷（几分钟渗透）、丙酮（快速渗透）、浓硝酸（氧化降解）、浓硫酸（90%+浓度快速降解）、DMF（可渗透）、乙酸乙酯（渗透较快）。丁腈手套的渗透时间因厚度而异——薄型（2-4 mil）渗透快，厚型（6-8 mil）渗透较慢。使用中一旦感到手套内湿滑或闻到化学品气味，说明已经渗透，应立即脱除更换。对于上述不耐受化学品，需选择层压膜手套（如Silver Shield/4H）或双层手套组合。
操作步骤：查阅SDS确认手套合适性→选择合适厚度和尺寸→检查无破损→戴手套操作→感到任何异常立即更换→脱除时避免污染皮肤
个人防护：丁腈手套（或根据化学品选择层压膜手套）
禁止事项：禁止用薄型丁腈手套长时间接触DMF/二氯甲烷;禁止手套内感到湿滑时继续使用;禁止使用有破损/变色/变粘的手套
废弃物处置：废弃手套按化学品污染类别处理（化学危废）
急救措施：化学品渗透到皮肤：立即脱除手套，大量清水冲洗
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Lab Safety Manual Appendix F; OSHA PPE Standard
来源机构：Cornell EHS / OSHA
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/chemical-safety/laboratory-safety-manual/appendix-f-glove-selection-guidance
标签：丁腈手套;渗透;手套选择;PPE
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8014
标题：什么情况下需要使用层压膜手套？如何使用？
类别：层压膜手套使用场景
子类别：手套安全
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：4
危险类型：高毒化学品;强渗透溶剂
适用场景：层压膜手套（Silver Shield/4H）的使用
问题：层压膜手套（如Silver Shield/4H/Beta-Safe等）由多层聚合物薄膜制成，耐化学品渗透性远超普通防化手套。适用于：1) 处理高毒化学品（如苯、DMF、二氯甲烷、汞化合物、氰化物）；2) 处理强渗透性溶剂；3) 混合溶剂体系（不确定性高时选用抗性最好的手套）。层压膜手套通常作为内层，外层戴丁腈手套提供机械保护和抓握力。使用后检查有无破损（针孔测试），可重复使用但需记录使用次数。层压膜手套的缺点是灵活性差、易刺破、成本高。
操作步骤：查阅SDS确认是否需要层压膜手套→选择合适尺寸→戴为内层→外层戴丁腈手套→使用后检查针孔→清洁后妥善保存
个人防护：层压膜手套（内层）+ 丁腈手套（外层）
禁止事项：禁止将层压膜手套作为外层单独使用（易破损）;禁止使用有针孔的层压膜手套;禁止在高毒操作中使用普通丁腈手套替代
废弃物处置：层压膜手套破损后按化学危废处置
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Lab Safety Manual Appendix F; NIH Chemical Safety Guide
来源机构：Cornell EHS / NIH
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/chemical-safety/laboratory-safety-manual/appendix-f-glove-selection-guidance
标签：层压膜手套;高毒防护;PPE;手套选择
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8015
标题：实验室什么情况下需要戴防割手套？
类别：防割手套的使用
子类别：手套安全
实验室类型：通用
风险等级：2
危险类型：割伤;锐器;玻璃碎片
适用场景：防割手套的选择与使用
问题：防割手套（通常为Dyneema或Kevlar材质）用于防止锐器伤害。使用场景：1) 清洗或拆卸玻璃仪器（尤其是磨口粘连时的拆卸）；2) 处理破碎玻璃器皿；3) 使用手术刀片/刀片进行切割操作；4) 安装/更换注射器针头（虽不应回套，但某些必要操作时）。注意：防割手套≠防化手套，不能防化学品渗透。防割手套应在防化手套外层或单独使用（根据是否需要防化）。破损的防割手套应立即更换（防割性能大打折扣）。
操作步骤：评估操作风险→选择合适尺寸→戴手套（如需要防化则内层先戴化学防护手套）→操作→检查手套有无破损→清洗或废弃
个人防护：防割手套;必要时配合防化手套
禁止事项：禁止用防割手套替代防化手套;禁止使用已破损的防割手套;禁止将防割手套暴露于强腐蚀化学品
废弃物处置：破损防割手套按普通垃圾或危废处理（取决于是否接触化学品）
急救措施：割伤：止血清洁消毒，必要时就医

来源标题：Cornell Lab Safety Manual Ch.3
来源机构：Cornell EHS

知识ID：KB-GAP-8016
标题：激光防护镜应该如何选择？
类别：激光防护镜选择
子类别：眼部防护
实验室类型：光学/物理
风险等级：5
危险类型：激光辐射;眼损伤;可见光/红外/紫外
适用场景：激光防护镜的选择
问题：激光防护镜必须与所用激光器的波长和功率匹配。选择要点：1) 查看激光器的安全标签确认波长（如1064nm Nd:YAG）和等级（Class 3B/4必须佩戴）；2) 防护镜标注光密度（OD值）——OD越高防护能力越强，但透光率越低；3) 不同波长需要不同的防护镜（532nm绿色防护镜对1064nm红外无效！）；4) 飞秒/皮秒超快激光需要特殊宽带防护镜；5) 防护镜镜架上标注适用波长范围，确认涵盖所用激光波长；6) 定期检查镜片有无划痕/褪色/老化。
操作步骤：确认激光波长和功率→查阅激光器安全标签→选择匹配OD值和波长的防护镜→检查镜片→佩戴→使用后妥善存放
个人防护：对应波长的激光防护镜
禁止事项：禁止使用不匹配波长的防护镜（几乎等于没戴）;禁止使用有划痕/破损/褪色的防护镜;禁止直视激光束（即使佩戴防护镜也不能直接看激光路径）
急救措施：激光防护镜划伤或褪色后失效，需更换
应急升级：眼损伤：立即就医眼科，告知激光波长和参数
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Lab Safety Manual Ch.15; ANSI Z136.1
来源机构：Cornell EHS / ANSI
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/chemical-safety/laboratory-safety-manual/chapter-15-laser-hazards
标签：激光防护镜;光密度;波长;PPE
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8017
标题：什么情况下需要佩戴面罩？和护目镜有什么区别？
类别：面部防护-面罩选择
子类别：面部防护
实验室类型：通用
风险等级：3
危险类型：飞溅;冲击;高温;紫外
适用场景：防护面罩的使用场景
问题：面罩（Face Shield）提供整个面部的防护，但不能替代护目镜！面罩+护目镜组合用于高风险场景：1) 大量强酸/强碱操作（>500mL）；2) 处理自燃或水反应性试剂（如钠、叔丁基锂、LAH）；3) 液氮或干冰/异丙醇浴的操作；4) 高压反应釜开釜操作；5) 打磨/切割操作（需抗冲击面罩）；6) UV消毒灯照射区域清洁（需防紫外面罩）。面罩不能替代护目镜——化学品溅入可能从面罩下方进入眼部，因此面罩下必须佩戴护目镜。
操作步骤：评估操作风险→佩戴护目镜→佩戴面罩（在护目镜外）→确认面罩下沿在颈前→实验操作→清洁面罩→妥善存放
个人防护：护目镜+面罩;实验服;手套
禁止事项：禁止仅戴面罩不戴护目镜;禁止在面罩有裂纹/黄化时继续使用;禁止使用普通塑料面罩替代防化面罩
废弃物处置：污染面罩清洁或作为危废处置
急救措施：化学品溅入面部：立即用安全淋浴冲洗15分钟，就医

来源标题：Cornell Lab Safety Manual Ch.3; OSHA PPE Standard
来源机构：Cornell EHS / OSHA
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/chemical-safety/laboratory-safety-manual

知识ID：KB-GAP-8018
标题：实验室什么时候需要C级化学防护服？正压防护服用在什么场景？
类别：正压防护服与C级防护
子类别：身体防护
实验室类型：生物/化学
风险等级：4
危险类型：高毒化学品;感染性气溶胶;缺氧风险
适用场景：正压防护服和C级化学防护服
问题：化学防护服分四级：A级（全封闭气密型，最高防护）> B级（全封闭供气型）> C级（化学防溅服+全面罩空气过滤呼吸器）> D级（普通工作服+基础PPE）。高校实验室最多用到C级。C级适用于：已知化学品浓度不超IDLH值、氧气充足(>19.5%)的环境，如大量化学品泄漏清理、高活性化学品处理。C级需配合全面罩+适当滤毒盒。注意：C级不能用于缺氧环境、未知化学品、或浓度>IDLH的场景。正压防护服（PAPR）用于BSL-3/4生物安全实验室，提供正压空气+全身防护。
操作步骤：评估化学品和风险→选择防护等级→着装（内层手套→防护服→外层手套→全面罩→呼吸防护）→检查密封→操作→在规定区域脱除→正确处理
个人防护：C级化学防溅服+全面罩+滤毒盒+双层手套+防化鞋套
禁止事项：禁止在IDLH环境或氧不足时使用C级（需A/B级）;禁止防护服破损时继续使用;禁止穿出污染区域
废弃物处置：一次性防化服作为危废处置;可重复使用防护服经去污处理后存放
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：OSHA 29 CFR 1910.120 HAZWOPER; EPA Levels of Protection
来源机构：OSHA
来源链接：https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.120
标签：防护服;C级;PAPR;PPE
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8019
标题：操作纳米材料需要什么特殊PPE？
类别：纳米材料操作PPE
子类别：特殊场景PPE
实验室类型：化学/材料
风险等级：4
危险类型：纳米颗粒;吸入;皮肤渗透;未知毒性
适用场景：纳米材料操作的PPE要求
问题：纳米材料（粒径<100nm）因其极小的尺寸可能通过肺泡进入血液循环或沿嗅觉神经入脑，其毒理学数据通常不完整。操作纳米材料（尤其是干燥粉末）的PPE要求：1) 呼吸防护：N95或P100过滤面罩（纳米颗粒可能穿透普通口罩），在通风柜或粉末称量柜中操作；2) 手部防护：丁腈手套双层，操作后确认无破损；3) 实验服：一次性实验服（纳米颗粒可能附着在纤维间难以洗净）；4) 眼部防护：护目镜（防粉尘）；5) 实验结束后湿式清洁（不可干扫——会使纳米颗粒重新悬浮）。
操作步骤：在通风柜/粉末称量柜内操作→佩戴N95+呼吸器→双层丁腈手套→一次性实验服→护目镜→实验后湿式清洁台面→正确处理废物
个人防护：N95/P100呼吸器;护目镜;一次性实验服;双层丁腈手套
禁止事项：禁止在通风柜外称量纳米粉末;禁止干扫（湿拖/湿擦）;禁止重复使用一次性实验服;禁止未做呼吸防护处理纳米粉末
废弃物处置：含纳米材料的废物双重密封，标注纳米材料种类，按化学危废处置
急救措施：吸入：移至通风处并就医
应急升级：纳米粉末泄漏：湿式清理，避免扬尘，收集后双重密封
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：NIH Safe Nanomaterials Handling; NIOSH Nanotechnology Guidelines
来源机构：NIH / NIOSH
来源链接：https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/topics/nanotech/
标签：纳米材料;PPE;呼吸防护;N95
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8020
标题：进行动物实验需要哪些PPE？
类别：动物实验PPE
子类别：特殊场景PPE
实验室类型：生物/医学
风险等级：3
危险类型：动物咬伤;过敏;人畜共患病;麻醉废气
适用场景：动物实验的PPE要求
问题：动物实验PPE根据动物种类和实验类型确定。基本要求：1) 动物设施专用实验服或隔离衣（不可穿出动物房）；2) 手套（咬伤高风险操作——如小鼠灌胃——加戴防咬手套外层）；3) 口罩/呼吸防护：对实验动物过敏者（常见大鼠尿液过敏）需加强呼吸防护；4) 护目镜或面罩；5) 专用鞋或鞋套。特殊场景：使用异氟烷等麻醉气体时——在通风柜或配备废气清除装置的环境中进行；非人灵长类实验——BSL-2+或BSL-3级别PPE。离开动物设施前必须脱除PPE并彻底洗手。
操作步骤：进入动物设施前换专用隔离衣→戴手套/口罩/护目镜→穿专用鞋→实验操作→脱除PPE→洗手→离开设施
个人防护：隔离衣;手套（防咬外层）;口罩;护目镜;专用鞋/鞋套
禁止事项：禁止将动物设施PPE穿出设施;禁止在动物设施内饮食/吸烟;禁止过敏人员未做额外防护接触过敏原;禁止被咬后不做医疗评估
废弃物处置：动物尸体/组织冷冻暂存后由专业机构无害化处理;针头/锐器入锐器盒
急救措施：咬伤/抓伤：立即流水冲洗，消毒，就医评估狂犬病/破伤风/其他感染风险
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：GB 19489-2008 实验室生物安全通用要求; Cornell Animal Biosafety Guidelines
来源机构：国家标准委 / Cornell EHS
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/biosafety-biosecurity/animal-biosafety
标签：动物实验;PPE;咬伤;过敏

知识ID：KB-GAP-8021
标题：含氟/氢氟酸的废液怎么处理？
类别：含氟废液处置
子类别：化学危废
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：4
危险类型：氟离子;腐蚀性;玻璃腐蚀;毒性
适用场景：含氟废液的安全处置
问题：含氟废液（如含HF、氟化物、含氟有机物的废液）特别危险。处置要求：1) 单独收集——含氟废液可腐蚀玻璃容器，须用PE/PP/PTFE塑料容器；2) 不可与酸性废液混合（HF+强酸释放更多HF气体）；3) 标注「含氟废液」及大致浓度；4) 含氟废液不可用玻璃瓶储存（长期会腐蚀玻璃导致泄漏）；5) HF相关实验中所有接触过HF的溶液（包括清洗液）都视为含氟废液。特别警告：HF中毒有延迟性（小面积接触可能数小时后才出现剧痛），所有含氟操作后洗手并监测皮肤。
操作步骤：用PE/PP/PTFE容器收集→单独密封保存→标注成分和HF浓度→满容器后交专业HF危废处置单位
个人防护：防酸手套（丁基橡胶或层压膜）;护目镜;面罩;实验服
禁止事项：禁止含氟废液与普通酸碱废液混合;禁止用玻璃容器盛放含氟废液;禁止倒入下水道;禁止敞口存放
废弃物处置：交有危废处置资质的专业单位（需具备HF处理资质）
急救措施：HF接触皮肤：立即大量水冲洗15分钟→涂抹2.5%葡萄糖酸钙凝胶→立即就医
应急升级：HF大量泄漏：疏散区域，通知专业应急人员（HF泄漏极度危险）
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：HF Waste Disposal Guidelines; Prudent Practices
来源机构：National Academies Press / OSHA
来源链接：https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK55873/
标签：含氟废液;HF;危废;特殊处置
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8022
标题：含氰化物的废液/废物怎么处理？
类别：含氰化物废液处置
子类别：化学危废
实验室类型：化学
风险等级：5
危险类型：氰化物;剧毒;产生HCN气体
适用场景：含氰化物废液的安全处置
问题：氰化物为剧毒物质，其废弃物处置安全要求极高：1) 含氰化物废液必须单独收集于专用废液桶（标注「含氰-剧毒」）；2) 绝对不可与任何酸性废液混合——氰化物遇酸释放HCN剧毒气体（一个呼吸即可致死）；3) 含氰化物废液桶存放在通风良好处；4) 废液桶保持密封；5) 氧化法预处理（漂白水/次氯酸钠在碱性条件下将CN⁻氧化为无害的氰酸根CNO⁻），但此项操作只能由经过专门培训的人员在通风柜内进行；6) 未经脱毒的含氰废液交专业危废单位处置。
操作步骤：含氰废液单独收集→标注「含氰-剧毒」→保持密封→不可混入酸→定期交专业单位处置（或由培训人员先做氧化脱毒预处理）
个人防护：丁腈手套;护目镜;实验服;在通风柜内操作
禁止事项：禁止含氰废液与酸混合（产生HCN毒气致死！）;禁止倒入下水道;禁止敞口存放;禁止在非通风区域打开含氰废液桶;禁止未经培训擅自做脱毒处理
废弃物处置：交有氰化物处置资质的专业单位
急救措施：氰化物中毒：立即移至通风处→如有亚硝酸异戊酯吸入剂可使用（破开用鼻吸入）→呼叫120→告知「疑似氰化物中毒」→不可口对口人工呼吸
应急升级：含氰废液与酸混合/HCN气体泄漏：立即疏散全部人员，报警（告知氰化氢泄漏），等待专业人员处理
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：GB 18597 危险废物贮存污染控制标准; Cyanide Waste Management
来源机构：生态环境部 / CDC
来源链接：https://www.mee.gov.cn/
标签：氰化物;剧毒;危废;特殊处置
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8023
标题：老旧设备中可能含有多氯联苯(PCBs)，应该如何识别和处置？
类别：含多氯联苯(PCB)废物处置
子类别：化学危废
实验室类型：化学/电气
风险等级：5
危险类型：多氯联苯;持久性有机污染物;致癌
适用场景：含PCBs废物处置
问题：多氯联苯(PCBs)是持久性有机污染物(POPs)，在老旧设备中可能存在。高PCBs风险设备：旧变压器油（1979年前）、旧电容器、旧荧光灯镇流器、旧显微镜浸油、旧导热油。若发现疑似含PCBs的老旧设备：1) 不要擅自拆卸或排油；2) 联系EHS进行PCBs检测（使用Cl-N-Oil试纸或送样分析）；3) 确认含PCBs后，设备和油均须按PCBs危废特殊规定处置（高温焚烧破坏）；4) PCBs泄漏区域需专业清理（PCBs可渗入混凝土并长期残留）；5) 含PCBs废物的处置需专门资质和转运许可。
操作步骤：识别疑似含PCBs设备→不擅自拆卸→联系EHS检测→确认后由专业人员处置→设备/油交PCBs专业处置单位
个人防护：操作疑似PCBs物质时：护目镜;丁腈手套;实验服;防止皮肤接触
禁止事项：禁止擅自拆卸疑似含PCBs的老旧设备;禁止将PCBs废物与普通危废混合;禁止用普通焚烧法处理（需>1200°C高温焚烧）
废弃物处置：交有PCBs处置资质的单位高温焚烧处理
急救措施：皮肤接触PCBs：立即用肥皂水彻底清洗
应急升级：PCBs泄漏：隔离区域，联系专业人员清理
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：EPA PCB Regulations 40 CFR 761; Stockholm Convention on POPs
来源机构：EPA
来源链接：https://www.epa.gov/pcbs
标签：PCBs;持久性有机污染物;危废;特殊处置
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8024
标题：实验室产生的放射性废物应该怎么处理？
类别：放射性废液处置
子类别：放射性废物
实验室类型：化学/医学
风险等级：5
危险类型：放射性污染;辐射;环境污染
适用场景：放射性废物的安全处置
问题：放射性废物处置受严格监管：1) 所有放射性废物（固体/液体/闪烁液/动物尸体）必须按核素种类和活度分类收集——短半衰期（如³²P, t₁/₂=14天）和长半衰期（如¹⁴C, t₁/₂=5730年）分开；2) 短半衰期废物暂存至活度衰变至本底水平后按非放射性废物处理（通常存放10个半衰期后检测）；3) 长半衰期废物交放射性废物处置机构；4) 含混合废物（同时含放射性和化学毒性，如闪烁液——含有机溶剂+放射性核素）需双重分类处置；5) 放射性废物暂存库有严格的辐射安全管理和保安措施。放射性废物管理必须在RSO指导下进行。
操作步骤：按核素和半衰期分类→使用专用放射性废物容器→贴标签（核素、活度、日期）→短半衰期暂存衰变→长半衰期交专业机构→填写放射性废物转移记录
个人防护：实验服;手套;必要时铅围裙和个人剂量计
禁止事项：禁止放射性废物与普通废物混合;禁止不同核素废物混合;禁止超暂存量存放;禁止未登记擅自转移;禁止非授权人员进入放射性废物暂存区
废弃物处置：按RSO规定的程序和放射性废物法规处置
急救措施：辐射暴露：脱去污染衣物，用辐射检测仪检测，按RSO指引处理
应急升级：放射性物质泄漏：疏散，封锁区域，报告RSO和应急响应
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：Cornell Radiation Safety Manual; 放射性废物管理规定
来源机构：Cornell EHS / IAEA
来源链接：https://ehs.cornell.edu/research-safety/radiation-safety/radioactive-materials
标签：放射性废物;核素;半衰期;RSO
语言：zh-CN

知识ID：KB-GAP-8025
标题：实验室危废桶上的标签应该怎么填写？
类别：危废标签规范填写
子类别：危废管理
实验室类型：通用
风险等级：2
危险类型：危废标识错误;信息缺失;法规不合规
适用场景：危险废物标签的正确填写
问题：危废标签必须完整准确填写，否则属于违规。必须标注的信息：1) 废物名称（不可只写「废液」——应写「含二氯甲烷的卤代有机废液」或更具体）；2) 主要成分及浓度（至少列出主要有害成分）；3) 危险特性（腐蚀性/毒性/易燃性/反应性）；4) 产生日期（开始收集的日期）；5) 产生实验室/房间号；6) 负责人姓名和联系方式；7) 危废类别代码。使用防水标签，用签字笔填写（不可用铅笔或可擦笔）。标签贴于废液桶侧面显眼位置，不可贴在桶底或桶盖上。满桶或过期未清理的及时联系危废转运。
操作步骤：在开始收集危废时即填写标签→信息完整准确→贴于桶身侧面→定期检查标签是否可读→满桶后通知转运
个人防护：手套（处理废液桶时）
禁止事项：禁止危废桶无标签;禁止标签信息不完整或不可辨认;禁止用缩写或含糊名称;禁止标签脱落/浸湿后不补换
来源类型：public_authoritative_source
来源标题：GB 18597-2001 危险废物贮存污染控制标准; 危险废物转移联单管理办法
来源机构：生态环境部
来源链接：https://www.mee.gov.cn/
标签：危废标签;法规;标识;管理
语言：zh-CN
